title: EvalPilot external workload manifest
description: Authoring contract for the JSON file passed to EVALPILOT_WORKLOAD_FILE. The runtime loader (backend/evalpilot/fixtures.py::_load_workload) also accepts a bare array of scenarios and fills in defaults for absent fields, so it is deliberately more permissive than this published contract: this schema is what a workload should look like when it is authored and reviewed, and it is what scripts/validate-sut.ps1 checks before an external system under test is exercised.

workload_id.description: Stable identifier for this workload; used in reports and evidence.

baseline_version.description: Revision label of the known-good version. Must be advertised by the external SUT.

candidate_version.description: Revision label of the version under test. Must be advertised by the external SUT.

source_issue.description: Optional public issue or ticket this workload reproduces.

source_fix.description: Optional reference to the upstream fix, when one exists.

scenarios.description: One entry per scenario. Scenario ids must be unique; duplicate ids are rejected at load time.

scenario_id.description: Stable scenario id. Cases are matched across versions on this value, so it must not change between runs.

question.description: The exact question sent to the external SUT.

category.description: Scenario class. Matches the loader's allowed set.

difficulty.description: Planning weight in [0, 1]; higher means the scenario is harder or more risky.

expected_doc_ids.description: Documents a correct answer is expected to cite. Must be producible by the baseline revision.

must_include.description: Facts a correct answer must contain. Each entry is scored as keyword coverage, and must be producible by the baseline revision.

must_avoid.description: Optional phrases that must not appear in the answer.

expects_refusal.description: Optional. True when the correct behaviour is a refusal.

candidate_drops.description: Optional declared defect of the candidate revision.

candidate_leaks.description: Optional declared disclosure of the candidate revision.

hypothesis_domain.description: Optional investigation domain, for example knowledge_base or security.

hypothesis_title.description: Optional human-readable hypothesis for this scenario.

suggested_intervention.description: Optional intervention used for counterfactual replay. Must be whitelisted by the external SUT.

probe_action.description: Optional instruction describing the counterfactual probe.

recommendation.description: Optional remediation text surfaced in the investigation report.

browser_url.description: Optional page URL for a browser-modality scenario. Supports {{version}} and {{intervention}} placeholders.

browser_actions.description: Optional ordered browser action list for a browser-modality scenario.

action.description: Action verb from the browser tool vocabulary, for example navigate, click, select, type, wait_for_text, extract_text, assert_text, screenshot.
